    - heading "Accessibility" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem: A group named by its title; Use memory is a switch with aria-checked and controls the note that unfolds
      - listitem: Category chips are a radiogroup with arrow keys and one tab stop; each group of memories is a labelled section
      - listitem: Every action button is named after its memory, e.g. "Forget “Prefers TypeScript…”"; actions also show on keyboard focus
      - listitem: Rows that are filtered out or folding away are inert, so the keyboard never lands on something hidden
      - listitem: "The status line in the last row is announced politely: counts, the forgotten memory with Undo, and editing hints"
    - heading "Motion" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem: Filtering folds the rows that don't match closed and fades them – nothing slides across the list
      - listitem: Forgetting folds the row away with a soft blur; Undo unfolds it at its old place and scrolls it into view
      - listitem: Pausing greys the text and a Paused tag fades in; the pause icon swaps to play
      - listitem: Counts on the head and in the last row roll to their new value; changing status text crossfades
      - listitem: Turning memory off dims the list and unfolds a short note; New memory unfolds into the editor in place of the button
      - listitem: With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement
